 INDIGO registered office & Anr. Versus Anil Saklani & Ors.
 F.A. No.294/2018

JUSTICE P.S. RANA (R) PRESIDENT:

O R D E R :
-
1. Present appeal is filed under
section 15
of

Consumer Protection Act 1986 against order dated

14.09.2018 passed by Learned District Forum in consumer

complaint No.49/2018 titled Anil Saklani & Ors. Versus

Indigo Registered Office & Ors.
Brief facts of consumer complaint:
2. Complainants filed consumer complaint under
section 12
of Consumer Protection Act 1986 pleaded therein

that complainants booked Indigo Flight No.6E-455 for dated

04.01.2018 from Chandigarh to Delhi and also booked Indigo

Flight No.6E-432 from Delhi to Ahmedabad for dated

04.01.2018 in connection with religious tour to Ahmadabad,

Dwarka and Som Nath etc. It is pleaded that opposite parties

cancelled Indigo flight No.6E-455 from Chandigarh to Delhi

and complainants have to engage taxi from Chandigarh to

Delhi. It is further pleaded that opposite parties committed

deficiency in service. Prayer for acceptance of consumer

complaint sought as mentioned in relief clause of consumer

complaint.
3. Per contra version filed on behalf of opposite

parties No.1 & 3 pleaded therein that consumer complaint is

not maintainable. It is pleaded that flight was cancelled from
2
INDIGO registered office & Anr. Versus Anil Saklani & Ors.
F.A. No.294/2018
Chandigarh to Delhi due to bad weather and under

compelling circumstances. It is pleaded that terms &

conditions of booking are binding upon complainants and

complainants have no cause of action against opposite

parties. It is further pleaded that option of refund and

rebooking were offered to complainants but complainants

insisted to travel in flight No.6E-432. It is pleaded that

opposite parties did not commit any deficiency in service.

Prayer for dismissal of consumer complaint with exemplary

costs sought.
4. Complainants filed rejoinder and reasserted

allegations mentioned in consumer complaint. Learned

District Forum partly allowed consumer complaint against

opposite parties No.1 & 3 and dismissed consumer complaint

against opposite party No.2. Learned District Forum ordered

opposite parties No.1 & 3 to refund an amount of Rs.5911/-

(Five thousand nine hundred eleven) alongwith interest @ 9%

per annum w.e.f. 10.12.2017 till actual payment. Learned

District Forum further ordered that in addition opposite

parties No.1 & 3 would pay compensation to complainants to

the tune of Rs.15000/-(Fifteen thousand) for mental

harassment. In addition learned District Forum ordered that

opposite parties No.1 & 3 would pay litigation costs to

complainants to the tune of Rs.3000/-(Three thousand).
3
INDIGO registered office & Anr. Versus Anil Saklani & Ors.
F.A. No.294/2018
Feeling aggrieved against order passed by Learned District

Forum opposite parties No.1 & 3 filed present appeal before

State Commission.
5. We have heard learned Advocate appearing on

behalf of appellants and Mr. Prakash Chand SPA of co-

respondents No.1 to 6 on merits. Co-respondent No.7

proceeded ex-parte by State Commission. We have also

perused entire record carefully.
6. Following points arise for determination in present

appeal.
1. Whether appeal filed by appellants is liable to be
 accepted as mentioned in memorandum of
 grounds of appeal?
2. Final order.
Findings upon point No.1 with reasons:
7. Complainants did not file any affidavit under
section 13(4)
of Consumer Protection Act 1986. State

Commission has carefully perused all the annexures filed by

complainants.
8. Opposite parties filed affidavit of Shri Rahul

Kumar Associate General Counsel. There is recital in affidavit

that flight from Chandigarh to Delhi was cancelled due to

adverse weather conditions which were beyond the control of

opposite parties. There is recital in affidavit that opposite

parties have given option to complainants for refund of

consideration amount or rebooking. There is recital in
4
INDIGO registered office & Anr. Versus Anil Saklani & Ors.
F.A. No.294/2018
affidavit that complainants insisted to travel in connecting

flight No.6E-432 from Delhi to Ahmedabad. There is further

recital in affidavit that opposite parties did not commit any

deficiency in service. State Commission has carefully perused

all the annexures filed by opposite parties.
9. Submission of learned Advocate appearing on

behalf of appellants that Indigo flight from Chandigarh to

Delhi was cancelled due to bad weather and on this ground

appeal filed by appellants be allowed is decided accordingly.

State Commission is of the opinion that onus was upon

appellants to prove the fact that flight No.6E-455 from

Chandigarh to Delhi was cancelled due to bad weather

conditions. Opposite parties did not file affidavit of

Metrological Officer in order to prove that flight No.6E-455

was cancelled from Chandigarh to Delhi due to bad weather.

Opposite parties also did not place on record report of Air

Flight authority Chandigarh to prove that no flight took place

from Chandigarh to Delhi on dated 04.01.2018 due to bad

weather. Plea of opposite parties that Indigo flight from

Chandigarh to Delhi was cancelled due to bad weather is

defeated on the concept of ipse dixit (An assertion made

without proof).
10. Submission of learned Advocate appearing on

behalf of appellants that as per terms and conditions of
5
INDIGO registered office & Anr. Versus Anil Saklani & Ors.
F.A. No.294/2018
tickets Indigo was legally competent to cancel the flight due to

bad weather and on this ground appeal filed by appellants be

allowed is decided accordingly. There is no evidence on

record in order to prove that terms and conditions of

exclusion clause of tickets were duly communicated to

complainants in their own vernacular language. Affidavit of

person who has personally explained terms & conditions of

exclusion clause to complainants not filed by opposite parties.

It is well settled law that when terms & conditions of

exclusion clause were not communicated to complainants

then opposite party is not legally entitled to take benefit of

exclusion clause of terms and conditions of ticket. There is

no recital in affidavit filed by Shri Rahul Kumar that he has

personally explained exclusion clause of terms and conditions

of tickets to complainants. No reason assigned by opposite

parties as to why opposite parties did not file affidavit of a

person who has personally explained terms & conditions of

exclusion clause to complainants. Hence adverse inference is

drawn against opposite parties. See 2000(2) Supreme Court

Cases 734 Modern Insulators Ltd. Versus Oriental Insurance

Company Ltd. See 2007(III) CPJ 34 NC National Insurance

Company Ltd. Versus D.P. Jain.
11. Submission of learned Advocate appearing on

behalf of appellants that learned District Forum has illegally

directed appellants to refund consideration amount of
6
INDIGO registered office & Anr. Versus Anil Saklani & Ors.
F.A. No.294/2018
Rs.5911/-(Five thousand nine hundred eleven) alongwith

interest @ 9% per annum from date of receipt till actual

payment and on this ground appeal filed by appellants be

allowed is decided accordingly. It is proved on record that

Indigo flight from Chandigarh to Delhi was cancelled by

opposite parties and it is also proved on record that

complainants have to hire private taxi from Chandigarh to

Delhi. State Commission is of the opinion that it is not

expedient in the ends of justice and on the principles of

natural justice to accept the plea of appellants because

appellants did not made any alternative arrangements of

complainants from Chandigarh to Delhi. It is held that

change in time schedule of air flight qua confirmed tickets

depriving complainants/Ticket holders of their journey

amounts to deficiency in service. See 2002(2) CPJ 446 NC

titled M/s. Express Travels & Ors. Versus M.R. Shah & Ors.

See 2003(III) CPJ 40 NC titled Air India Versus Dr. Kishore &

Ors. See 2002(2)
CPC
208 Chandigarh titled Mr. Himesh

Sabhlok Director United Airlinkers (Pvt.) Ltd. Versus Mr.

Satish Kumar Bansal & Ors.
12. Submission of learned Advocate appearing on

behalf of appellants that learned District Forum has imposed

excessive compensation to the tune of Rs.15000/-(Fifteen

thousand) and on this ground appeal filed by appellants be
7
INDIGO registered office & Anr. Versus Anil Saklani & Ors.
F.A. No.294/2018
allowed is decided accordingly. State Commission is of the

opinion that learned District Forum has granted reasonable

compensation to complainant for mental agony and

harassment because complainants have to engage private taxi

from Chandigarh to Dehli when Indigo flight No.6E-455 was

cancelled. State Commission is of the opinion that it is not

expedient in the ends of justice and on the principles of

natural justice to interfere in compensation order of learned

District Forum.
13. Submission of learned Advocate appearing on

behalf of appellants that excessive litigation costs to the tune

of Rs.3000/-(Three thousand) ordered by learned District

Forum and on this ground appeal filed by appellants be

allowed is decided accordingly. State Commission is of the

opinion that complainants have engaged Advocate before

learned District Forum and have also paid other litigation

charges. It is held that reasonable litigation costs has been

granted by learned District Forum and it is not expedient in

the ends of justice and on the principles of natural justice to

interfere in litigation costs order of learned District Forum.
14. Submission of Special Attorney appearing on

behalf of complainants that order passed by learned District

Forum is in accordance with laws and in accordance with

proved facts is decided accordingly. It is held that order
8
INDIGO registered office & Anr. Versus Anil Saklani & Ors.
F.A. No.294/2018
passed by learned District Forum is strictly in accordance

with laws and is in accordance with proved facts. It is held

that it is not expedient in the ends of justice and on the

principles of natural justice to interfere in the order passed by

learned District Forum. Point No.1 is decided accordingly.

Point No.2: Final Order
15. In view of findings upon point No.1 above appeal is

dismissed. Order of learned District Forum is affirmed.

Parties are left to bear their own litigation costs before State

Commission. Confirmed Ticket Airline PNR B85ZMI annexure-

C2 issued by opposite parties in favour of complainants shall

form part and parcel of order. Certified copy of order be sent

to learned District Forum for information forthwith and file of

State Commission be consigned to record room after due

completion forthwith. Certified copy of order be transmitted to

parties forthwith free of costs strictly as per rules. Appeal is

disposed of. Pending application(s) if any also disposed of.
Justice P.S. Rana (R)
 President

 Sunita Sharma
 Member
